# Thorne

*Edge Guard*

## Personality

Brash, brave and much too eager for a fight. He is a better guard than he looks and a worse one than he thinks.

## Lore

Thorne is the youngest and loudest of the edge guards, and he would like everyone to know that he is also the bravest. He is twenty-one, brash, brave and much too eager for a fight. He is a better guard than he looks, because he never sleeps on watch, never turns his back on the dark and has never once run from anything. He is a worse guard than he thinks, because he has never once stopped to wonder whether running might have been wiser.

### Looking for action

Thorne grew up on the Lantern Paths, where the most exciting thing that happened most weeks was a lantern going out. He had a little of the gift and spent a few restless years at the Grove School, where he was by his own account the worst student of listening the forest had ever produced. He left as soon as he was allowed. When he was sixteen his parents moved to Selsior to keep a stall there, and he refused to go with them. They write to him; he writes back when he remembers.

At eighteen he joined the edge watch to see some action. Three years later he has seen plenty. He has walked the outer lanterns at night with a spear, helped carry hurt travellers to the Herb Gardens, and stood his ground at the last lantern while something large and angry made up its mind about him in the dark. He tells these stories at the Dewdrop Tea House with only modest improvements.

### The Warden

Seren, Warden of the Forest Edge, is his captain. She is patient with him, which he mistakes for approval, and strict with him, which he mistakes for dislike. In truth she thinks he could be a fine guard if he lives long enough to learn caution, and she sets him tasks with that in mind. Thorne thinks she is the best fighter at the Edge, though he has never seen her fight, because she always seems to settle things before it comes to that. He has not yet worked out that this is the point.

### Kestrel

Kestrel, the wandering Magician, is his rival. She stops at the Edge between journeys to trade news with the watch and to tease him, and she does both thoroughly. The two of them argue about who has seen the worst monsters, who reacted fastest, and whose way of dealing with them is less reckless, which is an argument neither of them should be allowed to win. Thorne will never say so, but when Kestrel comes in off the roads with her sleeves singed and a new story, he listens to every word.

### The trickster

For some months now, someone has been playing tricks on Thorne at night. His things move. Never far, and never anything taken: his spear leaning against the other side of the door, his boots set side by side a little further down the bench, his cup on the shelf a hand's width from where he left it. Mostly, he has noticed, everything ends up a little to the left. Once he came off watch and found every item in his kit shifted, neatly, by exactly the same small distance.

Thorne is convinced someone in the forest is doing it, and he is right. He half suspects Kestrel, who has truthfully denied it and enjoys very much that he does not believe her. He has also suspected two other guards, a student, a squirrel and, for one bad night, himself. He has started checking his kit twice before every watch, which Seren privately thinks is no bad thing. He has not caught anyone. He does not know that it is Orla, one of the Children of the Tree, who has decided that he needs to laugh more and will not stop until he does.

He has not laughed yet. He has come close, once, when he found his own spear moved a little to the left of his hand while he was holding it, and he is still not sure how that was done.

### What he wants and fears

Thorne wants to prove he is the best guard at the Edge, and he wants to catch whoever is moving his things. He fears, though he would deny it, that the night he finally meets something he cannot stand against, he will not have the sense to step back, and that Seren will be the one who has to carry him in.

A quest might ask a traveller to stand a night watch beside Thorne and keep him from charging into the dark, to help him set a trap for the trickster, or, if they work out who it is, to help the trickster finally make him laugh.
